The default export documents the same object; only the metadata is read, so no code loads on the hot path. The six original metrics are declared by tenant_usage itself and cannot be redefined. Undeclared keys are logged and dropped, never thrown.

Told that a tenant's use of a metered quota passed one of its alert thresholds this month (Usage settings; 80 and 95 % by default), used it up, or went over it (docs/phases/53-setting-levels 53.9, D173). tenant_usage sends the usage.threshold / usage.overage webhooks itself; a listener does what the tenant's people see: tenant_subscription tells the tenant's owners and points them to the usage packs. Default export: QuotaAlertListener { quotaAlert(alert: { tenantId, metric, label, quotaKey, used, limit, percent, kind: 'threshold' | 'exhausted' | 'overage', threshold?, month }) => Promise<void> } (server/tenant_usage.extension-points.ts). Fired from the periodic usage job, at most once per metric, kind and threshold a month; best-effort (a failing listener is logged). Platform gate: a quota is the platform's billing, owed whatever the tenant switched on.

Installs the platform's default modules into a newly created tenant (docs/phases/25-marketplace/03-module-governance/01). Default export: { applyDefaultModules(tenantId) => Promise<{ installed: string[], skipped: { moduleId, error }[] }> } (TenantDefaultModulesProvider in server/tenant.extension-points.ts). Called while a tenant's defaults are seeded, AFTER the default plan (so a plan check sees the new plan), unless the caller asked to skip modules; every skipped module and any thrown error is recorded in the seeding report and never fails the creation. With no contribution, new tenants get only the code-level defaults.

Gives a newly created tenant its default plan. Default export: { assignDefaultPlan(tenantId) => Promise<void> } (TenantDefaultPlanProvider in server/tenant.extension-points.ts). Called while a tenant's defaults are seeded, unless the caller asked to skip plan or subscription seeding; an error is recorded in the seeding report and never fails the creation. With no contribution, new tenants have no plan.

(tenantId) => Promise<void>. Called BEFORE a tenant is deleted or a deletion is requested; a guard with an objection THROWS (409 recommended) and the deletion stops. Unlike almost every other point here it fails CLOSED: a guard that cannot be loaded, or is malformed, refuses the deletion with 503 — 'I cannot answer' is NOT 'no objection', because a silently skipped guard permits a write that cannot be undone. Guards run in order and the first objection stops the rest. Asked again right before the purge (the sweep and the fleet's purge-now): an objection that appeared during the grace period, or a guard that cannot answer, leaves the tenant PENDING_DELETION (the sweep asks again on its next run; purge-now answers BLOCKED, or fails on a 503). Zero contributions = no constraint. Declared so a tenancy primitive never imports the domains built on top of it: 'documents under legal hold' / 'payments still in flight' are the same question from other modules, each answered through this seam instead of a direct call into `tenant`. Which modules object, and which deliberately do not (debts, the tenant's own customer obligations, statutory retention): docs/phases/37-extensions/11-guards-that-object.md.

A header button of a tenant's page under Tenants (/admin/tenants/[targetTenantId], root tenant only) that opens another module's panel in a right-side drawer, the Devices page's pattern (no tab row, owner 2026-10-27): "Setting levels" (tenant_setting, docs/phases/53-setting-levels: where this tenant gets each module's accounts and settings from, set for this tenant alone). Implemented through the CLIENT slot 'tenant.detail.drawers': a contributor declares slots[] = { slot: 'tenant.detail.drawers', component, order, scope, permissions, props: { drawerId, label, labelKey } }; the component default-exports a function of { tenantId, targetTenantId, open, onCount, onClose } (common/ui/slot-drawers.component). It stays mounted while its drawer is shut and draws its panel only while open. The page shows a button only when its module is on and the viewer holds its permissions, isolates each in an error boundary, and opens the drawer whose drawerId is in `?panel=` on arrival. tenant imports none of the contributors (EXT-14).

A panel on the platform operator's tenant page (/admin/tenants/[targetTenantId], root tenant only), in the side column under the actions: what another module knows about that tenant (tenant_subscription: its plan, with the operator's plan change). Implemented through the CLIENT slot 'tenant.detail.panels': a contributor declares slots[] = { slot: 'tenant.detail.panels', component, order, scope }. Props received: { tenantId, targetTenantId } — tenantId is the root tenant the operator is on (build URLs with tenantPath(tenantId, ...) to the contributor's own GLOBAL operator routes), targetTenantId the tenant shown. A contribution shows its own load error rather than an empty state. The page imports none of them (EXT-14): a core module never calls a higher edition's route, the higher edition contributes here (41-ui-fixes/09 decision d).

Told what happened to a tenant, for a module that must report it elsewhere (the fleet agent's signed lifecycle receipts, docs/phases/02-fleet/05 section 7). Default export: { record(event: { tenantId, type: 'PROVISIONED' | 'SUSPENDED' | 'RESUMED' | 'DELETION_REQUESTED' | 'RESTORED' | 'PURGED' | 'LEGAL_HOLD_SET' | 'LEGAL_HOLD_CLEARED', occurredAt: Date, payload?: { commandJti?, counts?, hashes? } }) => Promise<void> } (TenantLifecycleSink in server/tenant.extension-points.ts). Called after the change is committed: a tenant was created, its status moved from ACTIVE to SUSPENDED or back, a deletion grace period started, a deletion was cancelled within it, the tenant was purged, or a legal hold was placed, extended, lifted or ran out (payload: G only, the hold's end in unix seconds and the sha256 of its reason). Best-effort: a sink that throws is logged and never fails the change. With no contribution, nothing is reported.

A header button of the Maintenance page (/admin/maintenance) that opens another module's panel in a right-side drawer, the Devices page's pattern (no tab row, owner 2026-10-27): "Announcements" (announcement, docs/phases/47-announcements: compose, schedule, preview, test send and withdraw announcements, and the window's own maintenance notices). Implemented through the CLIENT slot 'tenant.maintenance.drawers': a contributor declares slots[] = { slot: 'tenant.maintenance.drawers', component, order, scope, permissions, props: { drawerId, label, labelKey } }; the component default-exports a function of { tenantId, open, onCount, onClose } (common/ui/slot-drawers.component). The page shows a button only when its module is on and the viewer holds its permissions, isolates each in an error boundary, and opens the drawer whose drawerId is in `?panel=` on arrival. tenant imports none of the contributors (EXT-14).

One item of a tenant's onboarding checklist that another module owns (tenant_domain: dns_configured, a verified custom domain). The contribution's `key` is the step id. Default export: { done(tenantId) => Promise<boolean> } (TenantOnboardingCheck in server/tenant.extension-points.ts). Behaviour gate: a module that is off for the tenant has no step in its checklist. A check that fails or times out is listed as not done.

The stored files a module must still KEEP when the tenant is purged, because a law or a hold requires them for longer (issued invoices: Turkish Commercial Code art. 82, ten years; documents with an unexpired retention or under legal hold). Default export: (tenantId) => Promise<Array<{ storageKey, retainUntil: Date, reason } | { storageKeyPrefix, retainUntil: Date, reason }>> (TenantPurgeRetention in server/tenant.purge-retention.ts); the prefix form keeps every object under one key prefix without listing millions of keys. Answer only what is still retained (retainUntil in the future); an empty list keeps nothing. The purge's file step deletes every object of the tenant except the retained ones, which are marked on their uploaded_files rows and deleted by the daily sweep once retainUntil has passed; the sweep asks again first, so a hold that still stands keeps the file. Data gate (EXT-1): retention is a duty, so a module switched off for the tenant still answers. Fails CLOSED like tenant:deletion_guard: a contributor that does not load, throws, times out or answers something else defers the file step (no file of the tenant is deleted on that run and the sweep asks again on the next); the rest of the purge goes ahead. Who contributes and why: docs/phases/37-extensions/11-guards-that-object.md.

A teardown step of the tenant purge cascade that belongs to another module, such as cancelling the tenant's subscription with the payment provider. Default export: { purge(tenantId) => Promise<void> } (TenantPurgeStep). Best-effort: a step that throws is logged under its module's id and the cascade continues.

A step of a new tenant's seeding that belongs to another module, such as tenant_domain minting the tenant's <slug>.<wildcard> subdomain so it routes at once. Default export: { seed(tenantId) => Promise<void> } (TenantSeedStep in server/tenant.extension-points.ts). Run one after another in order, after the default plan, the default modules and the default settings. Platform gate: a brand-new tenant has no module activation seeded yet, so a behaviour gate would skip every step; only a module the platform banned, retired or does not have is left out. Best-effort: a step that throws is recorded in the seeding report as '<module>: <message>' and never fails the creation.

Told that a tenant's slug changed, for a module that keeps something named after it (tenant_domain renames the tenant's free <slug>.<wildcard> subdomain, so a rename keeps exactly one). Default export: TenantSlugChangeListener { slugChanged(event: { tenantId, previousSlug, slug }) => Promise<void> } (server/tenant.extension-points.ts). Called after the update committed, one listener after another. Best-effort: a listener that throws is logged and the rename stands, so a listener keeps its own periodic reconcile as the safety net. Platform gate: the subdomain is the platform's routing of the tenant, not a feature the tenant switched on.

The subscription health of tenants for the platform console's tenant list. Default export: { healthOf(tenantIds) => Promise<Record<tenantId, 'trialing' | 'active' | 'grace_period' | 'past_due' | 'expired'>> } (SubscriptionHealthProvider); a tenant with no subscription is absent from the answer. The list adds suspended and pending-deletion itself; with no contribution every other tenant reads no_subscription.

Told that a tenant entered or left SUSPENDED, for a module that gives the suspension its immediate effect beyond the request path (docs/phases/02-fleet/05 section 7 stage 7): tenant_session revokes the tenant's sessions, websocket_session fences the tenant's websocket handshakes and drops its live sockets. Default export: TenantSuspensionListener { suspensionChanged(event: { tenantId, suspended: boolean }) => Promise<void> } (server/tenant.extension-points.ts). Called after the status update committed, one listener after another: suspended=true when the status moved into SUSPENDED from any other status, false when it moved out of it. Best-effort: a listener that throws is logged and the status change stands (the request path refuses a suspended tenant on its own). Platform gate: ending a suspended tenant's sessions and sockets is a security action, owed whatever the tenant switched on.

A module whose UI texts are created at run time (the sidebar's renamed items, added workspaces and custom links of shell_menu) names their keys with their English source, so Platform -> Translations lists, counts, exports and imports them like any key and never flags their stored texts as leftovers. Default export: { sources() } implementing TranslationSourceProvider, answering [{ module, key, en }]; `module` must be the contributor's own id and the key must start with it. At most 5000 per provider; a provider that throws is left out of that answer. translation imports nothing of the contributing module.

Told after sessions are deleted (logout, sign out other devices, log out everywhere, password change, account deletion), with [{ userSessionId, userId, tenantId, sessionEndOrderedBy? }]; sessionEndOrderedBy (D249) names the modules whose session_end:order_source orders for that session were already recorded in the revoking transaction, whose hooks skip it. Default export: (revoked) => Promise<void>. For data bound to a session that must not outlive it — notification_push removes a native app's push token, which otherwise keeps delivering the account's notifications to a phone nobody is signed in on. Best-effort by contract: a hook that throws is logged and skipped, revoking a session must never fail because a satellite's cleanup had trouble. Sessions that merely expire are not announced.

A module that wants to hear every dispatched domain event. Default export: { key?, names?: string[], onEvent(tenantId, event, payload, meta?) } where meta is { actor?: { type, id } } (only the actor id travels; a flow that needs a name reads it with an enrichment node). dispatchEvent calls it BEFORE the plan gate, FIRE-AND-FORGET: dispatchEvent sits on the request path of ~50 modules, so a sink that is slow, broken or missing must never delay or fail a dispatch. A tenant without the feature_webhooks plan feature still reaches its sinks (the sink applies its own plan gate). Each sink is isolated; a throw is logged and dropped. Platform-scope events are pinned to the root tenant by dispatchPlatformEvent, so sinks hear them under the root tenant only.

A module declares a webhook event it emits, without editing webhook: one contribution per event, the contribution key is the event name (lower-case dotted segments, stable forever) and the static metadata is { scope: 'tenant' | 'platform', group, label, description }. The export is the module's <module>.webhook-events file, which lists the names for its emit sites; only the metadata is read, so building the catalog loads no code. The catalog (webhook.catalog.ts) is process-wide: the events of every installed module, whatever a tenant has switched on. Create, update and the manual trigger refuse an event no installed module declares for the tenant's scope (422); an update may keep an already-stored event whose module was removed. A dispatched event nobody declares is logged once and skips the endpoint lookup (event sinks still hear it). Two modules may declare the same event; the first by order wins and a declaration with a different scope is ignored with a warning.

modules.name: Account
modules.description: The signed-in person’s own account surface: the /me API and the "My Account" page. Owns no tables — it composes the user_* satellites, sessions, memberships and notifications behind one gateway so `auth` does not have to.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: AI firewall
modules.description: One security brain over the existing controls (an internal planning document): signals from every security control, a two-stage tree cascade in the request path (LightGBM scores an actor's behaviour against its own baseline on every request; the suspicious share goes to XGBoost, which classifies the attack from endpoint and HTTP metadata and decides allow, challenge or block for that one request), and a responder that acts through the owning modules' registered actions. Both models are evaluated in TypeScript inside this module and ship with the release; the deterministic controls stay the floor.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Announcements
modules.description: One message to every user on the right channels (an internal planning document): the platform operator to every tenant (chosen tenants, roles, plans, editions), a tenant admin to their own workspace. Popup (acknowledged once per person), toast, banner, the bell, mail, push and SMS; text per language with a fallback; send now or scheduled, expiry, withdraw; a send that keeps failing is given up, its sender told, and retried or withdrawn by hand; numbers per announcement. Maintenance windows make their own planned and unplanned notices on it.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: API Key
modules.description: Tenant-scoped API keys for programmatic access (hashed at rest, scope-bound).
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Admin Shell
modules.description: Persistent admin chrome: sidebar, top bar, workspace switcher, notification bell. Composes header-widget content from notification_inapp/tenant_branding/user — extracted from common (MIS-02) so the dependency-free primitives leaf no longer transitively carries those modules into every bundle.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Approval Queue
modules.description: Generic, entity-agnostic moderation / approval queue. Any owning module can route an entity through human review via the queue (keyed by entityType + entityId) with a tamper-evident per-tenant decision hash chain and an in-memory decision-handler hook. Open items are PENDING / IN_REVIEW / ESCALATED; terminal items are APPROVED / REJECTED, with a partial unique index enforcing at most one open item per entity and SLA-by-priority due dates. Every decision is recorded in the append-only audit log; submitters are notified in-app and (on a terminal decision) by email, and webhooks fire on each lifecycle event.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Audit Log
modules.description: Append-only audit trail for sensitive actions, stored per-tenant (platform events land on ROOT_TENANT_ID).
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Authentication
modules.description: Credential auth: login, register, password reset, email verify, OTP, TOTP. Coordinates user, user_session, user_security, notification_mail.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: ABAC Authorization
modules.description: Runtime attribute-based access control: a per-tenant policy PDP/PEP that decides permit/deny from subject/resource/action/environment attributes. Deny-overrides combining, RBAC fallback, short-TTL decision cache, and a decision simulator. Enforcement is opt-in — routes call authorize() alongside the existing tenant-session guard.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Automation integrations
modules.description: The types an automation integration is written against: nodes, choice lists and flow templates (`NodeContribution`, `NodeContext`, `ChoicesContribution`, `FlowTemplate` and what they reference). A module that adds to the automation engine keeps that code in its own folder and imports these types from here with `import type`, so it does not depend on the engine itself. Generated from the engine by scripts/gen-automation-contract.mjs; carries no code.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Common Primitives
modules.description: Dependency-free leaf module loaded by every other module: AppError + ErrorCode enum (with retryable flag, statusCodeFor/isRetryable helpers) plus shared locale, country, currency, timezone, Money, pagination and log-context primitives.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Dashboard
modules.description: The admin home screen and the widget platform behind it. A composition surface every workspace consumes and none owns -- sibling of app_shell rather than a business domain. Today it owns the /admin board and resolves which contributed widgets a caller may actually see; boards, widget definitions and the data-source seam arrive in later phases. Plan: an internal planning document.

modules.name: Feature Gate
modules.description: Plan-based feature gating as a leaf: owns the BOOLEAN/LIMIT policy, the grace-ceiling arithmetic and the Redis cache, but owns no table and knows nothing about plans or subscriptions. Where a tenant's entitlements come from is contributed through `feature_gate:entitlement_source`. With no source installed it does not gate at all.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Fleet Protocol
modules.description: Leaf contract package for the fleet federation (an internal planning document): canonical JSON, Ed25519 signing/verification of the message envelope, sealed boxes for PII-capable payload fields, and protocol version negotiation. Pure functions, no I/O, no database.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: I18n
modules.description: Application-UI translation RUNTIME — message resolution, {{var}} interpolation, the <I18nProvider>/useT client context, app-locale resolution and the app_locale cookie. Carries no reference data: language/country/currency catalogues and their pickers live in `localization`.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: IP Subnet
modules.description: Network primitives: subnet (CIDR) allowlist matching, address classification, and the shared types/enums for IP-based access control. Dependency-free leaf module.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Rate Limiter
modules.description: Sliding-window rate limiter + tenant-plan-based quota enforcement (seat/feature/usage limits).
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Localization
modules.description: Locale reference DATA — ISO languages, countries and currencies with their relationships (country ↔ languages ↔ currency), timezones, date/time formats, flag artwork, and the flag-aware pickers over them. Single source of truth, entering through one swappable data seam (server/localization.source). The translation runtime is a separate module: `i18n`.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Logger
modules.description: Winston-based structured logger. Use instead of console.* across the codebase.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: MCP server
modules.description: The platform's MCP (Model Context Protocol) host (docs/phases/57-mcp-server, ADR-0022): one stateless MCP server per contributing module at /api/mcp/<moduleId>, built per request from the tools modules register through mcp_server:tool. Each tool names a permission of its own module and runs only for a credential whose person holds it now (the phase 48 ceiling); tools a caller cannot use are not listed. Authenticated today by an API key of the tenant holding mcp_server.connect (MCP keys are API keys, made on the API keys page); OAuth for hosted connectors follows in 57.3. Every call is rate limited per credential, audited and seen by the AI firewall; tenant text in results is fenced as untrusted.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Module Lifecycle
modules.description: The single door for installing, activating, deactivating and purging a built-in module for a tenant: the install ledger, the one requires-closure, dependency guards, lifecycle hooks and the data purge. The marketplace storefront, plan changes and tenant provisioning all call it; none of them re-implements it. Whether a tenant may have a module is asked through `module_lifecycle:entitlement`, so this module never imports a billing rail.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Notifications
modules.description: The platform's notification dispatcher. Resolves recipient preferences, per-category opt-outs and ONE quiet-hours model once, then fans out to channel providers contributed through `notification:channel`. Security/OTP traffic is exempt from every recipient-controlled gate via an urgency flag.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: In-App Notifications
modules.description: In-app notification feed with unread counts. Consumed by the notification menu in the app shell.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Notification Log
modules.description: Unified outbound notification audit log across mail, sms, push, inapp channels.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Email Notifications
modules.description: Pluggable email sender (SMTP, SES, Mailgun, Postmark, Resend, SendGrid). EJS templates. BullMQ-backed queue.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Web Push Notifications
modules.description: Push notifications — Web Push (VAPID) and Expo (native apps): subscription storage + send.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: SMS Notifications
modules.description: Pluggable SMS sender (Twilio, Nexmo, Clickatell, NetGSM).
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Observability
modules.description: Sentry + Prometheus + OTel facade — plus ACTIVE uptime probing (SSRF-guarded HTTP monitors, debounced auto-incidents) and a public status/incident page (components, double-opt-in subscribers, live updates over the shared websocket gateway, maintenance read from tenant). Auto-tags every log/trace/metric with the active tenantId/userId/requestId via Logger AsyncLocalStorage context. Lazy-loaded — no-op when SENTRY_DSN / METRICS_ENABLED are off.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Organisation
modules.description: The shape of the tenant itself: its legal entities, the sites it operates from and the cost centers it slices itself by. The base every other business domain references — `tenant` is the SaaS account, `contact.Company` is an external counterparty, `organization` is the internal structure of that account.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Local Plugins
modules.description: The Core source of sandboxed plugins (OD-139): the platform operator uploads a plugin bundle, approves its sandbox grant and installs it for tenants, without the marketplace. Installed plugins contribute to external: true points (e.g. payment:gateway) through external:contributions.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Plugin Runtime
modules.description: Sandboxed execution runtime for untrusted community plugins (V8 isolates, brokered capabilities, no direct DB access).
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Process Host
modules.description: Leaf helper every non-Next sidecar process starts through: /healthz, /metrics, a Redis heartbeat into the process registry (proc:nodes:<kind>) and SIGTERM drain; the per-kind supervisor that forks and scales child processes by load within the cgroup budget (proc:sup:<kind>:<nodeId>); and the Redis leader lock for single-owner work (proc:leader:<kind>:<job>). Zero tables, no next/* imports; observability reads from it, never the other way round.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Redis
modules.description: Shared ioredis client + BullMQ connection helpers + Pub/Sub-safe createRedisConnection().
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Idempotency Keys
modules.description: Redis-backed idempotency-key store for safely retryable POST/PATCH operations.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Session-ending orders
modules.description: The transactional outbox of every "end this session" order (docs/audits/2026-11-03-redis-outage.md): a device kick for the MQTT gateway's iot:kicks stream, a websocket control order for the realtime gateway's ws:control:stream. An order is written in the same database transaction as the change that causes it (a device deleted, a credential revoked, a session revoked, a member removed, a tenant suspended), delivered right after the commit, and otherwise relayed every 5 s, oldest first, until Redis takes it; each carries a stable id so a reader acts on it once. A pending order older than a minute raises an alert and a metric; one the relay gives up on is kept as a dead letter for an operator. The hosts that end a person's access (user_session, tenant_member, tenant) record the orders of modules they cannot depend on (websocket_session's socket drops) through its point session_end:order_source, inside their own transaction (D249). A library and a relay: no UI, no tenant-facing route.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Menu
modules.description: The installation's admin sidebar, set by the sysadmin in Platform -> Menu instead of config/menu.ts: workspaces, groups, items and custom links per role and custom group, every label a translation key (English in the menu, other languages in the translation module's table), draft, preview, publish, revisions, export and import. One menu per installation (docs/phases/54-menu-editor).
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: File Storage
modules.description: Pluggable S3-compatible file storage (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, DigitalOcean Spaces, MinIO) with content-derived MIME validation and optional online virus scanning (VirusTotal).
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Telemetry
modules.description: Readings over time as a Core platform domain (docs/phases/42-telemetry): one row per message per retention class on db:time_series (TimescaleDB where present), the per-tenant key dictionary, the latest value per entity and key, 1-minute aggregates with hour and day rollups, retention per tenant and kind, the TelemetryWriter every kind writes through, the read service and API (latest, series by range: raw, minute, hour, day), a dashboard data source, a generic save node, the tenant purge and the plan-driven class switch. A module contributes an entity kind (telemetry:entity_kind) to store its readings; the IoT package registers iot_device on top of this store.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Tenant
modules.description: Tenant CRUD, lifecycle (active/suspended/deleted), soft-deletion service, and maintenance mode (planned downtime windows: scheduled/gradual/read-only, branded 503 page, status-page bridge). Foundation of multi-tenancy.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Tenant Branding
modules.description: White-label branding: logo, favicon, colors, font, custom CSS — read by the proxy/shell to render per-tenant chrome.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Tenant Domain
modules.description: Every tenant's free <slug>.<wildcard> subdomain, plus custom domains per plan (custom_domain / max_domains) with DNS verification (TXT/CNAME challenge) and suspension when the plan stops including them.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Tenant Invitation
modules.description: Email invitation flow: create / accept / decline / revoke. Bound to tenant_member on acceptance.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Tenant Member
modules.description: Tenant-scoped membership join table with roles (owner/admin/member) and per-member permissions.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Tenant Session
modules.description: Tenant-scoped session handling: bind a user session to a specific tenant, resolve tenant from request.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Tenant Settings
modules.description: Per-tenant key-value settings store — every method is tenant-scoped and rows carry tenantId. Modules declare their keys in *.setting.keys.ts; the service stores/reads them. Also hosts the admin settings console and per-tenant module enable/disable (module-activation).
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Tenant Usage
modules.description: Usage metric tracking per tenant (API calls, storage GB, seats). Source for plan-limit enforcement.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Guided tours
modules.description: Guided tours on the module pages. A module carries its tours as JSON (modules/<id>/tours/<tour>.tour.json, schema modules/tour/tour.schema.json): steps that highlight data-tour anchors in its pages, can span pages and move on when the reader clicks. The registry snapshot validates every tour (schema, anchors present in the code, admin routes, texts in the module's dictionary) and builds the list the browser loads. Every text is a translation key of the owning module, so tours are translated like any UI text (dictionaries or Platform → Translations, languages from localization, RTL mirrored). A Tours button in the top bar lists the tours of the page and the others; a tour is offered once on the first visit to its page. Done and skipped tours are remembered per browser. Draws with the kui-react Tour (Driver.js). No server routes, no tables.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Translations
modules.description: UI texts kept in the database on top of the module dictionaries in code: a language the code does not ship, or a corrected text, live without a deploy or a store release. Read order is database > JSON > English. Rows are per (locale, module, platform, key); platform NULL is shared by web and mobile.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: User
modules.description: Core user CRUD: create, find, update, deactivate. Foundation for every auth and tenancy flow.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: User Preferences
modules.description: Per-user preferences: theme, language, timezone, notification opt-ins.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: User Profile
modules.description: Profile fields (avatar, bio, locale, timezone) — separated from the user entity for read scalability.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: User Security
modules.description: Password hashing, account lock, TOTP secret, trusted devices, and the passkeyEnabled MFA-posture flag (passkey credentials live in auth_passkey).
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: User Session
modules.description: JWT access/refresh issuance + revocation, Redis-backed session cache, CRUD on UserSession rows.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Linked Social Accounts
modules.description: Per-user linked OAuth provider accounts (provider id, external user id, tokens).
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: Outgoing Webhooks
modules.description: Subscriber-configured outbound webhooks (tenant-scoped; root tenant carries platform-wide events), signed deliveries, retry+redelivery.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan

modules.name: WebSocket Gateway
modules.description: Shared realtime transport: a standalone Socket.IO gateway process that hosts one namespace per domain. Provides handshake tickets, presence/markers, a Redis pub/sub bridge, and ns-auth — domains register a RealtimeNamespace via the `websocket:namespace` extension point.
modules.author: Kuray Karaaslan
